Subject: Pricing follow-up: token economics & target $/1M benchmarking

Hi Liam / Sarah,

Great to meet earlier — thank you for walking us through the Acme use case and the throughput/latency constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps below so we're all aligned.

Recap of what you shared
- Expected steady-state: ~300-400M tokens / month (mix of input+output; peaks up to ~20 reqs/s in US region)
- Primary SLA needs: 95th p95 latency < 800ms for short-form generation; occasional longer-form jobs OK in batch
- Key decision criteria: unit economics ($/1M tokens), consistent latency, and predictable billing for forecasting

Acme asked: target $/1M tokens and how Redwood compares to OpenAI/Anthropic and open-model hosts. I'm attaching a quick comparison spreadsheet and would like to confirm the exact monthly token volumes (if you can share a CSV that helps us produce a tailored pilot).

Initial pricing guidance (ballpark) — high level only:
- Redwood Hosted (no commit): ~$18 / 1M tokens
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity, 3-12 month commit): ~$9 / 1M tokens (with 300M+/mo commit)
- OpenAI (public pricing equivalent): ~$20-25 / 1M tokens (depends on model family & context length)
- Anthropic (public pricing equivalent): ~$24 / 1M tokens
- Self-hosted / open-model hosts: ~$8-14 / 1M tokens depending on quantization, infra efficiency, and ops overhead

Notes: these are unit costs and don't capture quality differences (model family) nor reserved vs burst behavior. We can model a pilot price that blends a short-term discount with a committed tier if you want to test performance and cost side-by-side.

Ask / next steps
1) Can you share an estimate of monthly token mix (input vs output) and expected growth for the next 6 months? A CSV is easiest.
2) Would you be open to a 6-week pilot (reserved burst + host comparison)? If so, we can propose a pilot SKU: $10 / 1M tokens for first 3 months with a 300M/mo profile to validate latency and quality.
3) Any procurement or security questionnaires we should route to our compliance team?

Attaching: redwood_token_pricing_comparison.xlsx (high-level benchmarking). I've cc'd Marissa and Aditya for commercial/technical follow-up.

Thanks — happy to jump on a follow-up call this week if that's easiest.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

- Our current estimate (proof-of-concept telemetry) is ~350M total tokens / month (roughly 40% input, 60% output). Peak QPS tends to concentrate 10-30% of traffic in certain hours.
- Budget target: we're trying to land <$12 / 1M tokens if possible, since the business needs to hit a specific CAC / LTV threshold.

Liam — thanks for the CSV and the clear target. We'll ingest the CSV and produce modeled unit costs for your exact mix. Quick notes before we run the numbers:

Modeled benchmarking (preliminary) for Acme's ~350M/mo profile
- Redwood Hosted (pay-as-you-go): modeled ~$18 / 1M tokens (higher due to burst handling & no commit)
- Redwood Dedicated (3-12mo commit, reserved GPU pools): modeled ~$9 / 1M tokens (we can get to ~$8-10 range with longer commit and predictable tails)
- Proposed pilot offer: $10 / 1M tokens for first 3 months on a 300M/mo profile (hands-on onboarding + performance guardrails).

Competitive context (high-level):
- OpenAI public-equivalent: ~$20-25 / 1M tokens (varies by model & context)
- Anthropic public-equivalent: ~$22-26 / 1M tokens
- Open-model hosts / self-hosted: can be as low as ~$8 / 1M tokens if aggressively quantized and using spot infra, but ops/latency/quality tradeoffs are non-trivial

Key tradeoffs to highlight for Acme:
- Latency: Redwood Dedicated offers predictable p95 behavior and caching/KV reuse for repeated prompts, which materially reduces effective per-interaction cost and improves UX
- Quality: model family choice matters — lower unit cost models may not match the quality of the baseline you were demoing
- Predictability: reserved capacity smooths monthly spend and avoids surprise burst costs

Next steps I'll take this morning
- Marissa and I will run the CSV through our cost model and produce a per-scenario workbook (hosted vs dedicated vs pilot) with assumptions called out.
- I'll route any procurement questions to Aditya for a short template of terms/SOW for pilot.

If $10 / 1M for a 3-month pilot at ~300M/mo is acceptable to you, we can draft a one-page pilot SOW and target kickoff within 2 weeks. Does that sound reasonable?

Thanks — looping Marissa/Aditya to own the commercial/ops details.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
